extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of ancient political history
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts and summarizes criteria, warnings, and normative judgments about what makes republican constitutions and political institutions stable, just, and prosperous, as discussed in a historical account of Roman republican development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Well-ordered constitution fosters capable citizens and prosperity
rubrics_metrics.description: A regular, well-ordered constitution will never fail to bring forth men capable of conducting the national councils and arms; it is of infinitely more importance to national happiness to abound in good merchants, farmers, and manufacturers... than to multiply what are called great statesmen and great generals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize institutional arrangements that cultivate broad civic and economic virtues (merchants, farmers, manufacturers, lawyers, priests, physicians, philosophers) over concentrating prestige in a few military or political leaders. A well-ordered constitution produces competent administrators and milder social outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certainty and publicity of law
rubrics_metrics.description: It is a miserable servitude... where the law is uncertain and unknown; and it is only under the security of certain and known laws, that arts, sciences, agriculture, commerce, and trades can ever be made to flourish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Laws should be clear, public, and stable. Legal uncertainty undermines economic and cultural development and enables arbitrary power; codification and public record (e.g., the recording of senate acts) are safeguards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear allocation of functions among assemblies and offices
rubrics_metrics.description: As it was not with any precision determined by law what business should be done in one assembly, and what in the other, the patricians and plebeians... were in danger of rendering the administration of the state a continual scene of contradictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constitutional rules must precisely define which bodies handle which matters to avoid institutional conflict and contradictory decrees. Ambiguity about jurisdiction (e.g., what the comitia versus the tribes may decide) invites factional conflict and instability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid multiple overlapping legislative sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Hence three distinct sources of laws — decrees of the senate, acts of the centuries, and resolutions of the tribes — a source of division, distraction, and tumult, which never ceased to issue streams till the authority of the senate was wholly destroyed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concentrated or at least coherent legislative authority is preferable to competing, overlapping lawmaking bodies; multiple independent law sources can erode authority and produce chronic constitutional crisis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Codification of judicial procedure and legal protections
rubrics_metrics.description: The people pursued... a new code of laws which would regulate the forms of judicial proceedings; the decemvirs presented a number of laws... containing a summary of the privileges of the people, the crimes to be punished, and the forms of judicial proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish clear legal codes and procedural rules to secure rights and standardize justice. However, codification must be pursued for the sake of justice and fair process, not merely to gain political advantage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit and check magistrates' power and duration
rubrics_metrics.description: The power of a magistrate was supposed to determine only by his own resignation. The decemvirs, taking advantage of this defect in the constitution, continued the exercise of their power... until the people expelled the decemvirs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Magistracies must have well-defined term limits and mechanisms to prevent usurpation or extension of temporary powers. Temporary commissions vested with excessive or indefinite authority risk permanent usurpation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid cruel and arbitrary private-law sanctions
rubrics_metrics.description: Bankruptcy was made a crime; without any distinction between fraud and misfortune, exposed the insolvent debtor to the mercy of his creditors, who might put him to death, dissect, or quarter him, and distribute his members among them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Laws concerning debt and personal status should distinguish misfortune from fraud and avoid dehumanizing punishments. Excessively harsh private-law sanctions foster popular unrest and demands for remedial reform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Religious toleration and restraint from penalizing private worship
rubrics_metrics.description: In private every family were free to worship the gods in their own way; and in public, though certain forms were required, yet there was not any penalty annexed to the omission of them... This was probably the source of that wise and humane toleration which does so much honour to the Romans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowing private religious freedom and limiting coercive public penalties in matters of worship fosters social tolerance and reputational advantage among nations; leave certain religious offenses to the offended deity rather than the state when feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate emerging social groups through shared deliberative roles rather than separate sovereign bodies
rubrics_metrics.description: Equity required that the plebeians should have a voice in the legislature; but instead of becoming a branch of it... they obtained a separate and independent power of legislation. Hence the intricacy of this constitution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When incorporating previously excluded groups, prefer inclusion within existing deliberative structures (shared voice, veto, participation) rather than creating parallel sovereign institutions that produce countervailing and conflicting authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guard against corruption from imperial conquests and provincial wealth
rubrics_metrics.description: The success of the Roman arms abroad became the source of a ruinous corruption at home... citizens contended for offices as the road to lucrative appointments abroad; they brought back a profusion of wealth ill acquired, and the habit of arbitrary and uncontrolled command.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design accountability mechanisms for provincial governors and limit pathways by which military/administrative service can be transformed into unchecked private enrichment. Prevent office-holders from converting command abroad into oligarchic domestic power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit the political influence of a moneyed/contracting class
rubrics_metrics.description: The knights, or the equestrian order... being persons possessed of estates... formed, between the senate and the people, an intermediate rank... and constituted a species of moneyed interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that economic intermediaries (contractors, tax farmers, merchants) form vested interests that can distort politics; institutions should check undue influence of moneyed classes on legislation and administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid creating a dependent, clientelistic populace through gratuitous distributions
rubrics_metrics.description: The city was gradually crowded with a populace, who, tempted with the cheap or gratuitous distribution of corn... flocked to Rome. There they were corrupted by idleness and indigence... A turbulent populace tyrannized, in their turn, over the masters of the world, and wreaked... the evils which they themselves had so freely inflicted on mankind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public welfare measures must be designed to avoid creating permanent dependency that clientelizes voters and enables demagogic manipulation; preserve social and economic structures that encourage productive activity rather than idle dependence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use electoral/tribal design as a safeguard against unrepresentative influence
rubrics_metrics.description: The censors had taken the precaution to confine all citizens of mean or slavish extraction to four of the tribes... These were called the tribes of the city, and formed but a small proportion of the whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electoral geography and franchise design (tribal or districting methods) can be used to limit the disproportionate influence of corrupt or unrepresentative groups, but such measures carry their own normative costs and must be justified carefully.
